question: The three-tier system of Panchayati Raj was first recommended by the ________ in 1957.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Balwant Rai Mehta Committee**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed by the Government of India in 1957 to examine the working of the Community Development Programme (1952) and the National Extension Service (1953) and to suggest measures for better working of these programmes.
 
• The Committee recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system at the village, block, and district levels.
 
• This structure was aimed at decentralizing power and ensuring greater participation of people in the administration of rural areas.
 
• The three tiers proposed were: Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zila Parishad at the district level.
 
• The recommendations of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee were accepted by the Government, and the Panchayati Raj system was first introduced in Rajasthan in 1959.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Panchayati Raj system is a system of rural local self-government in India.
 
• The system was constitutionalized through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992.
 
• The Amendment provided a constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions and brought them under the purview of justiciable part of the Constitution.
 
• It added a new part IX to the Constitution titled "The Panchayats" and a new Eleventh Schedule covering 29 subjects within the functions of Panchayats.
 
• The Act aims to provide a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj for all States having a population of over 2 million, to hold Panchayat elections regularly every five years, to provide reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women, and to appoint a State Finance Commission to make recommendations regarding the financial powers of the Panchayats.
